title: Attention fuzz & failure-injection harness
body:
Summary:

Short: this doc describes a lightweight fuzz + failure-injection harness we built to exercise attention kernels (FlashAttention, paged attention, and fused ops paths) under adversarial scheduling, quantization noise, and resource pressure. Goal: find reproducible correctness and stability failures that don't appear in normal perf runs and produce actionable mitigations (safety checks, backoff policies, kernel guards).

Why we did it (motivation):
- We keep seeing rare correctness/NaN/soft-failure reports from customers on mixed workloads where kernels switch between Flash and paged variants. Usually these are single-digit-per-million requests but highly correlated with heavy KV-cache churn and small-batch bursts.
- Traditional microbenchmarks hit throughput/latency but don't stress race windows, prefetching fallthrough paths, or fusedop reorder cases.
- We need reproducible minimally-invasive test harness to run in CI and on staging clusters to catch regressions before rollout.

Hypotheses we want to test (non-exhaustive):
1) Race between prefetch fallthrough and fusion handshake triggers memory aliasing and occasional NaNs when fusedops reorder is enabled.
2) Quantized int8 kernels are sensitive to small scaling changes combined with sequence truncation; under random drop-in failure injection (partial KV fetch) we get off-by-one indexing that leads to garbage outputs.
3) Kernel switchpoints (Flash -> Paged) executed mid-inference can leave stale pointers to scratch buffers causing silent corruption for multi-request coalesced batches.
4) Schedulers that do opportunistic coalescing will increase small-batch starvation microbursts and expose accumulation rounding issues in fused softmax.

Harness architecture (high level):
- Fuzzer controller (python) that spawns many short generation requests with randomized parameters: seq_len, batch_shape (including ragged batches), dtype (fp16/int8), use_kv_cache true/false, prefetch_hint on/off, fusedops set/clear, quant-scale variation.
- Failure injection hooks (C++ shim loaded into runtime via LD_PRELOAD in staging) that can:
  - Drop Nth prefetch request (simulate partial read)
  - Delay kernel launch by X ms to create handoff races
  - Flip a sparse set of floats to NaN with a low probability
  - Force a kernel fallback path (simulate OOM in Flash kernel)
- Lightweight observer: captures perf counters (nvprof/cupti-lite), kernel names and timings, per-request checksum (hash of tokens + few output floats), and stack traces for crashes.
- Reproducer capture: when a checksum mismatch or NaN observed, harness captures full request representation and an invocation script that replays the exact sequence and LD_PRELOAD config.

Test matrix (example sets we ran):
- baseline: seq_len 32/128/512, batch 1..8, fp16, no failures (sanity)
- coalescing stress: small-batch bursts (1000 1-batch jobs then big job), fusedops=on, prefetch_hint varying
- fuzz: randomized choices for kernel flags, seed logged, injected delay 0..50ms at kernel handoff points
- quantized: int8 kernels with scale offsets +/- 5% and random drop-in NaNs at 1e-6 per-element
- paged-path heavy: force Flash kernel to fail on 10% launches to force paged fallback under load

Notable observations (condensed):
- Repro case A (coalescing + delay): we observed a deterministic NaN when a coalesced batch of shape [3,1..] had one request switch to paged path mid-kernel. Stack shows fused-softmax executed on a stale scratch buffer. Reproducer captured; root cause: buffer reuse indexing wasn't zeroed on fallback.
- Repro case B (partial prefetch drop): repeated partial KV reads produced consistent probability mass loss in softmax outputs (sum < 0.999) leading to downstream token hallucinations. This was correlated with a race where the prefetch completion callback didn't mark a 'ready' bit before fusion handshake.
- Repro case C (quant noise + small seq): int8 kernels produced outlier tokens when quant scale drift > 4% and small batch coalescing applied. Mitigation via stronger scale clamping reduced occurrences.
- Heisenbug: an intermittent OOM-like fallback that only appears when cuBLAS workspace is concurrently used by unrelated kernels; failure injection delay reproduced it reliably.

Representative logs & quick traces (snippets):
- Kernel timeline (from cupti-lite):
  T0: flash_attn_launch(seq=128,batch=4) 2.1ms
  T1: prefetch_read_kv(req=42) delayed by 35ms (injected)
  T2: fused_softmax(buf=0x7f5a1c, size=4096) returns NaN at element 2047
  Checksum pre: 0x1a2b3c4d check_post: NaN -> flagged

- Reproduce command (auto-generated):
  export LD_PRELOAD=/staging/failure_inject.so 
  ./run_inference --model t5-lg --seed 374829 --seq-len 128 --batch 4 --fusedops=on --kv-prefetch=on 

Repro strategy and triage workflow: 
1) When harness flags a problem, it writes a reproducer package with: input.json, env.txt (LD_PRELOAD config), runtime flags, profiler dump.
2) Triage owner (rotation weekly) attempts local reproduce on a tiled staging machine (same driver/CUDA). If reproducible, file a JIRA with artifact and assign to kernel owner.
3) For correctness issues, create a targeted unit test in core/attention/tests that asserts output checksums across fused/paged/flash code paths.
4) For flakiness that only reproduces under heavy co-tenancy, run a 24h burn-in on a 4-GPU staging node with harness enabled.

Mitigations and short-term fixes implemented so far (timeline):
- 2025-06-12: added a guard to zero scratch buffer on Flash->Paged fallback (reduced NaN cases by ~98% in harness runs).
- 2025-06-20: introduced stronger quant-scale clamping for int8 kernels when batch size < 4. Reduced outliers by 80% in fuzz runs.
- 2025-07-03: landing of failure injection harness as a staging-only feature behind a flag (--enable-attn-fuzzer).

Open questions / next experiments:
- How much do different GPU generations (A100 vs H100 vs consumer Ampere) affect the observed race windows? Need matrix across driver versions.
- Should we add a lightweight checksum step in the runtime after kernels return (cheap fp16-based approximate sum) as a canary to detect silent corruption before returning to customers? Trade-off is cost/latency.
- Explore integrating harness into nightly CI with a low-probability long-run job to catch regressions early. Cost estimate: ~3-4 GPU-hours/night.

TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] Evan: add unit test for scratch buffer zeroing across fallback paths (PR reference in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Marco: run fuzz harness across h100 staging region and record difference matrix (target by 2025-08-09).
- [ ] Sofia: draft RFC for optional runtime canary checksum and perf cost estimate (due 2025-08-01).
- [ ] Priya: land repro packaging into perf-ingest bucket and automation to create JIRA when checksum mismatch (in progress).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could randomize block-size alignment in synthetic tensors to stress misaligned copy paths.
- Consider a lightweight telemetry flag for customers who opt-in to fuzzing on their dedicated clusters to surface rare kernel regressions without shipping failure injection to prod.
- Slack thread: #serving-attn has 3 strands about this: link pinned in confluence page.

Appendix (quick commands used to drive harness locally):
- python harness/runner.py --mode fuzz --duration 6h --concurrency 40 --target staging-t4x2 --outdir /tmp/attn-fuzz/20250718
- LD_PRELOAD overrides implemented in c/failure_inject.c (simple hooks on cudaLaunchKernel, cuMemcpyAsync, and our runtime prefetch API).

If you want to run this: ping me or check confluence page (linked_artifacts). Repro package for the most common NaN case is saved as /perf-artifacts/repro-20250718-nan-case.tgz.

End of doc.
